subject: maths
title: Index notation, squares and square roots

scenes.heading: Index notation, squares and square roots
scenes.sub: A shortcut for multiplying the same number again and again
scenes.say: Writing three times three times three times three is slow. Index notation gives you a shortcut. In this video you'll also meet square numbers and square roots.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A square of tiles 7 tiles wide uses 7 × 7 = 49 tiles
scenes.breaks: Only square numbers make a perfect tile square, but every positive number has a square root.
scenes.say: Picture square floor tiles. A square seven tiles wide uses seven times seven, which is forty-nine tiles. Forty-nine is a square number. Going backwards, from forty-nine tiles to a side of seven, is finding the square root.
scenes.caption: Picture square floor tiles. A square 7 tiles wide uses 7 × 7 = 49 tiles. 49 is a square number. Going backwards, from 49 tiles to a side of 7, is finding the square root.

scenes.heading: Index notation
parts: the base: the number being multiplied
scenes.say: Two to the power of four means two times two times two times two, which is sixteen. The two is the base, the number being multiplied. The four is the index, which tells you how many twos. It is not two times four.

scenes.heading: Squares and square roots
scenes.say: Squared means to the power of two. Five squared is twenty-five. Learn the square numbers: one, four, nine, sixteen, twenty-five and so on. The square root undoes squaring. The square root of sixty-four is eight. And the square root of forty is between six and seven, because forty is between thirty-six and forty-nine.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Evaluate √(3² + 4²).
scenes.say: Evaluate the square root of three squared plus four squared. Do the powers first: three squared is nine, four squared is sixteen. Add them to get twenty-five. The square root of twenty-five is five.

scenes.heading: Don't mix them up
scenes.say: Watch out for these traps. Two to the power of four is not two times four; it's sixteen. The square root of sixteen is not half of sixteen; it's four. And three squared plus four squared is nine plus sixteen, which is twenty-five.

Quick recap. The index tells you how many times to multiply the base. Squared means power two, and cubed means power three. The square root undoes squaring. And powers come early in the order of operations. Now try the practice questions!
